units.source: Templates
A template in Trilium serves as a predefined structure for other notes, referred to as instance notes. Assigning a template to a note brings three main effects:

__TRILIUM_PH_0__Attribute Inheritance__TRILIUM_PH_1__: All attributes from the template note are __TRILIUM_PH_2__inherited__TRILIUM_PH_3__ by the instance notes. Even attributes with __TRILIUM_PH_4__ are inherited by the instance notes, although only inheritable attributes are further inherited by the children of the instance notes.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Content Duplication__TRILIUM_PH_1__: The content of the template note is copied to the instance note, provided the instance note is empty at the time of template assignment.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Child Note Duplication__TRILIUM_PH_1__: All child notes of the template are deep-duplicated to the instance note.
Example__TRILIUM_PH_0__
A typical example would be a "Book" template note, which might include:
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Promoted Attributes__TRILIUM_PH_1__: Such as publication year, author, etc. (see __TRILIUM_PH_2__promoted attributes__TRILIUM_PH_3__).
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Outline__TRILIUM_PH_1__: An outline for a book review, including sections like themes, conclusion, etc.
__TRILIUM_PH_0__Child Notes__TRILIUM_PH_1__: Additional notes for highlights, summary, etc.
Instance Note__TRILIUM_PH_0__
An instance note is a note related to a template note. This relationship means the instance note's content is initialized from the template, and all attributes from the template are inherited.
To create an instance note through the UI:

For the template to appear in the menu, the template note must have the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ label. Do not confuse this with the __TRILIUM_PH_1__ relation, which links the instance note to the template note. If you use __TRILIUM_PH_2__workspaces__TRILIUM_PH_3__, you can also mark templates with __TRILIUM_PH_4__ to display them only in the workspace.
Templates can also be added or changed after note creation by creating a __TRILIUM_PH_0__ relation pointing to the desired template note.

To specify a template for child notes, you can use a __TRILIUM_PH_0__ relation pointing to the appropriate template note. There is no limit to the depth of the hierarchy — you can use __TRILIUM_PH_1__, __TRILIUM_PH_2__, and so on.

Changing the template hierarchy after the parent note is created will not retroactively apply to newly created child notes.__TRILIUM_PH_0__For example, if you initially use __TRILIUM_PH_1__ and later switch to __TRILIUM_PH_2__, it will not automatically apply the new template to the grandchild notes. Only the structure present at the time of note creation is considered.
Default parent for new notes__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Templates > Default parent for new notes

units.source: A template can gather the notes created from it in one place, instead of having them land wherever they happen to be created. To do so, add a __TRILIUM_PH_0__ relation to the template note, pointing at the note that should hold the instances, for example a __TRILIUM_PH_1__Person__TRILIUM_PH_2__ template pointing to a __TRILIUM_PH_3__People__TRILIUM_PH_4__ note. The relation can also be set by clicking the template badge next to the note title and selecting __TRILIUM_PH_5__Template properties...__TRILIUM_PH_6__, then picking a note under __TRILIUM_PH_7__Default location of created notes__TRILIUM_PH_8__.
units.context: Templates > Default parent for new notes

units.source: Adding the relation several times places the new note in every target, as __TRILIUM_PH_0__Cloning Notes__TRILIUM_PH_1__. The relation can also be inherited (e.g. from a folder holding several templates), in which case a relation owned by the template itself replaces the inherited one. The default parent is only inherited from the template's ancestors in the tree: a template created from another template does not adopt that template's default parent.
units.context: Templates > Default parent for new notes

units.source: The default parent is used whenever a note is created from the template through the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Choose note type__TRILIUM_PH_1__ dialog:
units.context: Templates > Default parent for new notes

units.source: Via the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Create note__TRILIUM_PH_1__ option of the __TRILIUM_PH_2__-completion in a __TRILIUM_PH_3__Text__TRILIUM_PH_4__ note
units.context: Templates > Default parent for new notes

units.source: Via the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Create note__TRILIUM_PH_1__ or __TRILIUM_PH_2__Create child note__TRILIUM_PH_3__ options of the note search (new tab or __TRILIUM_PH_4__Internal (reference) links__TRILIUM_PH_5__), but only if the dialog's __TRILIUM_PH_6__Location__TRILIUM_PH_7__ field is left empty.
units.context: Templates > Default parent for new notes

units.source: Creating an instance note from the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note Tree__TRILIUM_PH_1__ context menu (__TRILIUM_PH_2__Insert child note__TRILIUM_PH_3__, __TRILIUM_PH_4__Insert note after__TRILIUM_PH_5__) still creates it at the chosen place.
units.context: Templates > Default parent for new notes

units.source: Unlike the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note Inbox__TRILIUM_PH_1__, which holds quickly captured notes until they are sorted, the default parent is meant as the instances' permanent location.
units.context: Templates > Default parent for new notes

units.source: Regarding note types__TRILIUM_PH_0__

By default, newly created notes are __TRILIUM_PH_0__Text__TRILIUM_PH_1__ notes. If a parent note defines a __TRILIUM_PH_2__ pointing to a template of a different type (e.g. a Code note), the behavior depends on how the new note is created:
If no note type is explicitly chosen (e.g. the + button in the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note Tree__TRILIUM_PH_1__), the template is applied and the new note takes the type and content of the template.
If a note type is explicitly selected (e.g. __TRILIUM_PH_0__Note Tree__TRILIUM_PH_1__ → __TRILIUM_PH_2__Insert note after__TRILIUM_PH_3__ / __TRILIUM_PH_4__Insert child note__TRILIUM_PH_5__):
If the selected type matches the template's type, the template is applied.
If the selected type differs, the template is disregarded entirely — the new note is an empty note of the selected type.
Selecting a specific template from the creation menu always takes precedence over __TRILIUM_PH_0__.
Default title for new notes__TRILIUM_PH_0__
units.context: Templates > Default title for new notes

units.source: A template can also give its instances a default title, using the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ label. To set it without editing the label by hand, click the template badge next to the note title and select __TRILIUM_PH_1__Template properties...__TRILIUM_PH_2__, which checks the expressions as you type and previews the resulting title. See __TRILIUM_PH_3__Default Note Title__TRILIUM_PH_4__ for details.
units.context: Templates > Default title for new notes

units.source: Additional Notes__TRILIUM_PH_0__
From a visual perspective, templates can define __TRILIUM_PH_0__ and __TRILIUM_PH_1__ attributes, allowing all instance notes (e.g., books) to display a specific icon and CSS style.

Explore the concept further in the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Demo Notes__TRILIUM_PH_1__, including examples like the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Relation Map__TRILIUM_PH_3__, __TRILIUM_PH_4__Task Manager__TRILIUM_PH_5__, and __TRILIUM_PH_6__Day Notes__TRILIUM_PH_7__.

Additionally, see __TRILIUM_PH_0__Default Note Title__TRILIUM_PH_1__ for creating title templates. A __TRILIUM_PH_2__ on a template note is passed on to its instances like any other label, so it names the children of each instance rather than the instances themselves; to name the instances, use __TRILIUM_PH_3__.
